newsitem.title: ISRAEL: FOCUS-Tel Aviv Wednesday bourse trade in question.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Tel Aviv Wednesday bourse trade in question.

text.p: The Tel Aviv Stock Exchange on Tuesday decided not to hold the main session of trading in the 100 most liquid stocks after a strike by Bezeq Israel Telecom workers wreaked havoc with communications.
A bourse spokeswoman said brokerage houses and banks could not get through to the exchange.
She said it was not yet known whether trading would resume on Wednesday.
"Today we won't have an answer, only tomorrow morning," she said.
A Bezeq union official said workers would obey a labour court order and return to their jobs on Wednesday morning but it would take "a pretty long time" to restore full telephone service.
Thousands of Israeli homes and businesses have been off line since Bezeq repair crews stopped answering calls a week ago.

The morning session of call market trading known as the Meretz took place as usual. The Meretz session determines the market trend and executes small orders while the bulk of trading in the 100 most liquid stocks takes place in the later session known as the Mishtanim.
Bonds traded as well as options on the Maof blue chip index and the dollar.
